intro: Enter a base and an exponent to raise a number to a power. The exponent can be a whole number, a negative number, a decimal or a fraction like 2/3, and the steps show what that exponent means.

formula.label: Fractional exponent
formula.note: The bottom of the fraction is the root, the top is the power.

howItWorks: For a positive whole exponent, the base is multiplied by itself that many times. Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1. A negative exponent means take the reciprocal: work out the positive power, then put 1 over it.

A fractional exponent is a root. The bottom number of the fraction tells you which root to take, and the top number is the power. So a^(1/2) is the square root of a, and a^(2/3) is the cube root of a, squared. Decimal exponents work the same way, because 0.5 = 1/2 and 1.5 = 3/2.

A negative base with a fractional exponent whose bottom number is even, like (−4)^(1/2), would need an even root of a negative number. No real number squared gives a negative, so the calculator reports it as not a real number.

example.title: A negative fractional exponent
steps: The exponent is negative, so take the reciprocal: 27^(−2/3) = 1 ÷ 27^(2/3).
The bottom of the fraction is 3, so take the cube root: ∛27 = 3.
The top of the fraction is 2, so square it: 3² = 9.

mistakes.title: Multiplying the base by the exponent
Thinking a negative exponent makes the answer negative
mistakes.text: A negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative number. 2⁻³ = 1/8 = 0.125, not −8.

mistakes.title: Reading a half power as halving
mistakes.text: 16^(1/2) is the square root of 16, which is 4. It is not 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

mistakes.title: Losing the brackets on a negative base
mistakes.text: (−2)⁴ = 16 because the minus is part of the base. −2⁴ = −16 because only the 2 is raised to the power and the minus is applied after.

faqs.q: Why is any number to the power 0 equal to 1?
faqs.a: Look at the pattern: 2³ = 8, 2² = 4, 2¹ = 2. Each step down divides by 2, so the next step is 2⁰ = 2 ÷ 2 = 1. The same thing happens for any non-zero base.

faqs.q: What does a decimal exponent mean?
faqs.a: Turn the decimal into a fraction. 4^1.5 = 4^(3/2), which is the square root of 4 cubed: 2³ = 8.

faqs.q: Why is (−4)^(1/2) not a real number?
faqs.a: It asks for the square root of −4, and no real number times itself gives a negative answer. A cube root is different: (−8)^(1/3) = −2, because (−2)³ = −8.

faqs.q: Is a^(m/n) the same as the n-th root of a to the power m?
faqs.a: Yes. You can take the root first or the power first. For 8^(2/3), the cube root of 8 is 2 and 2² = 4, or 8² = 64 and the cube root of 64 is 4.
